Name: Adobe Premiere Pro
Description: Control Premiere timelines and Lumetri Color with your Ulanzi device.

Actions.Name: Quick Export
Actions.Tooltip: Export the current sequence in Premiere or add it to the Media Encoder queue. Each press creates a new export without overwriting existing files.

Actions.Name: Playhead
Actions.Tooltip: Turn the dial to move the playhead frame by frame; hold and turn to move faster. Movement stops at the start or end of the sequence.

Actions.Name: Clip Trim
Actions.Tooltip: Select a clip on the timeline first. Ripple editing adjusts its In or Out point and moves later clips along with it. Rolling editing moves the edit point between this clip and the next. Unsupported clips stay unchanged.

Actions.Name: Timeline Zoom
Actions.Tooltip: Turn clockwise to zoom in or counterclockwise to zoom out, centered on the playhead.

Actions.Name: Dial Parameter Switch
Actions.Tooltip: Press to switch the parameter controlled by dials in the same group. This only selects a parameter; it does not change the image.

Actions.Name: Lumetri Dial
Actions.Tooltip: Turn to adjust the current parameter; hold and turn to switch parameters; press to reset the current parameter to its default.

Localization.queueExport help: Add the current sequence to the Adobe Media Encoder export queue. With Start Media Encoder queue automatically enabled, exporting starts immediately, including other waiting jobs. Otherwise, the job is only added to the queue; start it manually in Media Encoder. Each press adds a new job without overwriting existing files. Check export progress in Media Encoder.
Localization.timelineJog help: Turn to move the playhead frame by frame; hold and turn to move faster. Movement stops at the start or end of the sequence.
Localization.trimControl help: Select clips on the timeline first. Supports one clip, or one video and one audio clip with matching starts and ends. For rolling edits, the next pair must also be adjacent and aligned. Transitions, speed changes, captions and complex sync-lock arrangements are not supported.
Localization.timelineZoom help: Turn clockwise to zoom in or counterclockwise to zoom out. Zoom centers on the playhead; if it is not visible, the mouse position or timeline center is used. Keep Premiere in the foreground with the timeline visible. Requires 64-bit Windows 10 version 2004 or later, or macOS 13 or later.
Localization.parameterSelect help: Press to switch the parameter controlled by dials in the same group. Each group has one active parameter at a time. This only selects a parameter; it does not change the image.
Localization.parameterDial help: Turn to adjust the selected clips. Hold and turn clockwise for the next parameter or counterclockwise for the previous one. Press without turning to reset the current parameter to its default (100 for saturation, 0 for others). For keyframed clips, only the value at the playhead changes; other keyframes stay unchanged.
Localization.Preset search help: Favorites shows presets starred in Premiere's Preset Manager. All shows every preset, with favorites first. Custom shows only presets in the chosen folder and its subfolders. Switching sources keeps your current preset until you select another from the list. To add presets, put .epr files in the custom folder and click Refresh.
Localization.Trim press help: Press the dial to cycle the movement step: 1 → 5 → 10 frames.
Localization.Group help: Give this button and the dials it should control the same group number. Different groups work independently.
Localization.Lumetri behavior help: Adjusts the first Lumetri Color effect on each clip. If exactly one clip is selected and has no Lumetri Color effect, turning the dial adds it automatically. Before adjusting multiple clips together, manually add Lumetri Color to each one.
Localization.Lumetri safety help: Adding Lumetri Color automatically is not officially supported by Premiere. If the plugin cannot confirm that it is safe to proceed, it stops without making arbitrary changes to your clips.
Localization.Saturation range help: Ranges: saturation 0–200 (100 is the original saturation), exposure -5–5, other parameters -100–100.
